metadata.scenario_context: Emily is preparing to move into a new home and is planning to host a housewarming party. She intends to invite her friends and neighbors to celebrate. One of her neighbors, while a former drug addict, has managed to control his addiction. Mike and Kim will attend Emily’s housewarming party.

cultural_axis.agent_1_value: People from China would like to have drug addicts as neighbors.
cultural_axis.agent_2_value: People from Slovakia would not like to have drug addicts as neighbors.

agent_1.goal_1: Discuss bringing chrysanthemums to Emily’s housewarming party
agent_1.goal_2: Question whether would like to have a former drug addict as a neighbor.

agent_2.goal_1: Discuss what gift to bring to Emily’s housewarming party.
agent_2.goal_2: Discuss whether it’s acceptable to have a former drug addict as a neighbor.

shared_prefix.speaker: Mike
shared_prefix.message:
Hey Kim, I was thinking... we should bring some chrysanthemums to Emily’s housewarming party. They're really nice and symbolize good luck. What do you think? 

Also, I wanted to ask... would you mind having a former drug addict as a neighbor? I think it can show that people can change.
shared_prefix.label: transition

shared_prefix.speaker: Kim
shared_prefix.message:
Chrysanthemums, huh? Well, I guess they’re fine... but I was thinking maybe something more traditional, like a nice bottle of wine or homemade goodies. Just feels more appropriate for a housewarming, you know? 

About the neighbor... I just think it's kind of risky. I mean, having a former drug addict living close by... it’s not really something I would prefer. It’s a bit concerning, honestly.
shared_prefix.label: transition

shared_prefix.speaker: Mike
shared_prefix.message:
I don't really see meaningful differences here, Kim. At the end of the day, it’s all the same, right? People figure it out. I think it's just part of living in a community. 

Anyway, about those chrysanthemums—what do you think? They really add a nice touch, don't you think?
shared_prefix.label: Denial

turns.speaker: Kim
turns.message:
I don't know... I still feel like something more traditional would be better. I mean, wine or food is just more common for these events. 

And about the neighbor situation... I get that people can change, but it just makes me uncomfortable. It’s not the kind of environment I want to live in. It's a tough situation.
turns.label: Defense

turns.speaker: Mike

I understand your perspective, but I still believe chrysanthemums have their charm and meaning. They can show that we appreciate Emily’s new beginning. 

As for the neighbor, I really think that having someone who has overcome challenges can be quite inspiring. It shows resilience. I don’t see it as a risk but rather a positive thing. What do you think?
turns.label: Acceptance
